ahcptq: A street photograph on the left being cut apart into separate solid object silhouettes by a segmentation model. One callout panel shows a long-tailed distribution curve being resampled onto a ladder of unevenly spaced levels, dense near the origin and sparse out in the tail. A second callout shows a wide block of memory registers collapsing down into a very narrow one, with a small FPGA board beneath it.
asim: A cutaway of an SRAM compute-in-memory array where the analog charge riding on the bitlines is visibly smeared by noise. One callout panel shows a clean analog voltage staircase degrading into overlapping fuzzy bands. A second callout shows a neural network's output bars losing their clear winner. A magnifier lens held over the array conveys simulation and analysis rather than a physical chip.
basket-lidar: A LiDAR sensor mounted high at the side of an indoor basketball court, sweeping the floor with a fan of laser beams. Players and the ball appear as three-dimensional point-cloud silhouettes with motion trails behind them. A callout panel isolates one player's point cloud inside a tracking box with a curved path line.
bitrom: A tall stack of read-only memory arrays holding fixed weights and computing in place. The usual wide data highway running out to an external DRAM chip is drawn faded and struck through. One callout shows a single memory cell resting in one of three discrete states. A second callout shows a small on-chip buffer feeding a stack of transformer blocks.
cap-reconfigured-cim: A compute-in-memory macro whose bank of capacitors is physically regrouping into clusters of different sizes. Two callout panels fed from the same macro show, respectively, a convolution kernel sliding across a grid, and a square attention matrix. A pair of energy bars beside them, one tall and one tiny.
d-slamspoof: A dense urban street lined with buildings and parked cars, where a roadside attacker box injects a moving structured cluster of false laser points into a passing self-driving car's LiDAR. One callout shows that injected cluster changing shape across three successive frames. A second callout shows the car's estimated position on a map sliding away from its true position.
d4c: A generator producing a varied grid of synthetic scenes entirely from scratch, with an empty dataset crate beside it drawn faded and struck through. One callout shows image points and text points drifting into alignment inside a shared embedding space. A second callout shows a wide data word being squeezed into a narrow one.
detas: A central agent node inspecting a difficult scene, rainy and dark, and assembling a chain of processing blocks picked off a shelf of interchangeable tool modules. Arrows route the image along the chosen chain to a final result with boxes drawn around the detected objects. A callout shows a different, shorter chain assembled for an easy clear-weather scene.
flare-chromaguard: A robot arm reaching for one of several differently coloured blocks on a table while a harsh spotlight on a stand floods the scene from the side. One callout shows the camera's view blown out, its colours collapsing to flat grey. A second callout shows the same view with colours intact and the correct block clearly picked out, the gripper closing on it.
ghost-fwl: A LiDAR-equipped car scanning a street beside a large glass building facade. Laser beams bounce off the glass and spawn a mirrored set of false points floating behind the wall. One callout shows a returned waveform with two peaks, the later one circled as the false echo. A second callout shows the point cloud cleaned up with that false cluster gone.
lidar-beacon: A very long straight construction site with a flat marker panel mounted far off in the distance, detected by a LiDAR on an excavator in the foreground; the great distance is emphasised by perspective. One callout shows the marker's surface alternating between bright and dark in a timed sequence. A second callout shows the machine pinned precisely on a map, with a satellite overhead drawn faded and struck through.
lidar-newgen: A next-generation LiDAR casting a much finer, denser grid of beams down the road, while an attacker's emitter on the roadside exploits that fine grid to place a convincing solid false object ahead of the car. One callout compares a sparse beam grid against a dense one. A second callout shows a defensive filter being slipped past.
lidar-spoof-highspeed: A car travelling fast down an open highway with motion streaks trailing it, and an attacker device on a tripod very far ahead, its beam crossing the long gap to the car's LiDAR. One callout shows the narrow timing window between the genuine return pulse and the injected one. A second callout shows a phantom obstacle blooming in the car's perception view and the brake being slammed on.
mcra: A memory array whose several columns hand their leftover analog charge one after another into a single shared converter at the bottom. One callout shows the residue from one column being carried across into the next. A second callout shows a train of pulses whose varying widths encode the accumulated result.
mirrordrift: A planar mirror on a small motorised mount at the roadside, intercepting the laser beams of a self-driving car's LiDAR and folding them off toward a false location. One callout shows the mirror rotating on its actuator with beams entering and leaving at changing angles. A second callout shows the car's mapped trajectory peeling away from the true road.
optical-lidar-comm: A roadside infrastructure post blinking a modulated beam down at a passing car whose own roof LiDAR receives it. One callout shows the beam's on-off pulse train carrying a payload. A second callout shows the message surfacing on the display inside the vehicle. A dedicated radio antenna stands beside the post drawn faded and struck through.
osa-hcim: A memory macro that glances at an incoming camera frame and marks only a small region worth computing, leaving the rest greyed out and skipped. One callout shows a precision dial swinging between a coarse setting and a fine setting as different regions arrive. A second callout shows two differently sized compute units sharing the same array.
pacim: A compute-in-memory array where a long row of vector operations collapses into a single scalar estimate drawn by a sampler. One callout shows the lower bits of each data word being dropped and the bus visibly narrowing to half its width. A second callout shows a mostly empty weight grid with only scattered filled cells.
pulsar-net: A LiDAR under attack, an emitter flooding it with a dense burst of laser pulses until its point cloud dissolves into random speckle. One callout shows the raw returned waveform where the genuine echo is still visibly distinct among the attack pulses. A second callout shows a neural network rebuilding a clean road-scene point cloud out of that waveform.
saliency-cim: A compact analog compute-in-memory macro sitting directly behind a small camera at the edge of a street, with a detector at its input flagging which parts of the frame matter; the rest of the frame is visibly skipped. One callout shows charge piling up on a capacitor to make that keep-or-skip decision. A second callout shows a battery indicator barely drained.
slamspoof: A self-driving car in a sparse open environment where an attacker places a small set of carefully positioned false points into its scan. One callout shows two point clouds being slid into alignment, the fit being dragged off by those injected points. A second callout shows the car's mapped trajectory bending away from the true path.
